question: GQ-001
subject: a rule of mine was blocking the goal, not protecting it
the_blocker: "--skip-sqlite refuses --strict" — my own rule, written one turn earlier

why_it_was_wrong.what_strict_actually_is: ONE line: exit 3 if findings exist. An exit-code switch, not a coverage switch.
why_it_was_wrong.the_real_danger: a skipping run standing in for the run that GATES A PUSH — which is the hook, not the self-test
why_it_was_wrong.verified_before_changing_it: lifted the rule on a scratch copy; a falsified declared number still exited 3 under --skip-sqlite

the_narrower_rule.now: refuses when GATING=1, which the pre-push hook sets

result.coverage_unchanged: removing the audit's --strict exit on a scratch copy makes 10 of 15 cases FAIL — they still detect a broken gate

what_this_closes: Last turn: "the self-test still cannot run on every push at 367s." It runs on every push now, and the quick suite got FASTER than when it ran one fewer suite.
still_off_the_hook: gates-are-load-bearing.sh, ~300s, replays the chain once per gate. Runs from npm run check:all.
correction_2026_08_05: This file said gates-are-load-bearing.sh is "~300s, replays the chain once per gate". The 300s was carried forward, never re-measured. Re-measured today it ran in 57s — and that was WRONG for a worse reason: audit-verify-chain.mjs had joined the chain as the FIRST gate, and it reports chain-names-missing-gate for any gate absent from disk. So every removal was caught by the guard in 0s rather than by the removed gate. The suite reported "7 load-bearing" while testing one thing seven times. Excluding the guard gives the honest result: 289s, 6 load-bearing.
